text:
Justin Brazeau is 6'7", undrafted, and paid his way to the NHL in Providence, which tells you most of what you need to know about how he plays. Four games into his season, he has a goal (against Boston, the team that gave him his start) and is getting fourth-line minutes, about 10:43 a night.

Four games is nothing, and his on-ice chance numbers so far (33% of the expected goals at five on five) are too small a sample to read. The longer track record is more useful. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.1 wins above replacement last season, almost all from even-strength offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows exactly where it comes from: 8.5 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net, 99th percentile among forwards, and an unusual habit of setting up plays from behind the net (21% of his setups, against 8% for a typical forward). He won't beat anyone with speed. He'll beat them by standing where it hurts.
